files.lesson.md: --- order: 9 unit: shapes node: AC9M7SP02 n3 uses: [AC9M7M05 n2] # the angle sum of a polygon title: Polygons summary: "A polygon is named by its number of sides (pentagon 5, hexagon 6, octagon 8, decagon 10). It is regular when all its sides and all its angles are equal, and concave when a corner points in." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Stop signs are octagons, honeycomb cells are hexagons, and a star is a polygon with corners that point in. What makes some of them regular?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8283 url: http://127.0.0.1:8283/index.html readySelector: "#gclass" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: shape.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A hexagon with one corner pointing in: concave. Its sides are not all equal, so it is irregular too." } explainClip: query: { code: "@shape.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Regular, or not" say: "Regular means equal sides and equal angles." clip: - caption: { text: "A square: the regular quadrilateral.", say: "A square is the regular quadrilateral." } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Five equal sides and five equal angles: a regular pentagon.", say: "One more side: a regular pentagon." } - click: More sides - expect: { selector: "#gclass", contains: "Regular pentagon" } - wait: 1000 - caption: { text: "Move one corner: still a pentagon, but irregular.", say: "Move one corner. Still a pentagon, but now irregular." } - click: Move A right - click: Move A right - expect: { selector: "#gclass", contains: "Irregular pentagon" } - wait: 1200 --- A **polygon** is a closed shape with straight sides. Its name counts the sides: | Sides | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Name | triangle | quadrilateral | pentagon | hexagon | heptagon | octagon | nonagon | decagon | A polygon is **regular** when **all its sides are equal and all its angles are equal**; otherwise it is **irregular**. It is **convex** when every corner points out (every angle less than 180°), and **concave** when at least one corner points in (an angle more than 180°). ## Predict: six equal sides ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to whether equal sides alone make a regular hexagon shows whether they know regular needs equal angles too." check: type: predict q: "A hexagon has six equal sides. Must it be a regular hexagon?" options: ["No: its angles might not be equal", "Yes: equal sides make it regular", "Only if it is convex"] actual: "No. Squash a regular hexagon and the sides stay equal but the angles change. Regular needs equal sides and equal angles." ``` Picture pushing two opposite corners of a regular hexagon towards each other. ## Run: a corner that points in ```step stage: run insight: "Changing the number of sides and dragging one corner inwards shows regular, irregular and concave as properties of any polygon." try: { playground: board, starter: "shape.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Make a hexagon with one corner pointing in (concave). Is it regular? Was your prediction about sides and angles right?", when: "n = 6 and v = 0", explain: "A corner pointing in has an angle over 180°, so the angles are not all equal: a concave polygon is never regular." } ``` **More sides** and **Fewer sides** change the shape; it starts regular. Then drag a corner. ## Investigate: names and properties ```step stage: investigate insight: "Names count sides; regular needs equal sides and equal angles (Kim checks only the sides); concave means a corner points in." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each polygon to its number of sides." pairs: - ["pentagon", "5"] - ["hexagon", "6"] - ["heptagon", "7"] - ["octagon", "8"] - ["decagon", "10"] explain: "Pent- five, hex- six, hept- seven, oct- eight (an octopus has eight arms), dec- ten." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#kim" text: "Kim decides whether a rhombus is regular. Click the line where her reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: regular-sides-only explain: "Line 3: regular needs equal angles too, and 60° and 120° are not equal. The only regular quadrilateral is a square." - check: type: question q: "How can you tell that a polygon is concave?" options: ["At least one corner points in, with an angle more than 180°", "It has more than six sides", "Its sides are not all equal", "It has a right angle"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A regular octagon has eight sides and is convex.", "That makes it irregular, not concave.", "A square has right angles and is convex."] explain: "A concave polygon has a corner that points in: a reflex angle, over 180°." ``` ### Count, then check Here is the routine for naming a polygon. ```worked \text{6 sides} \Rightarrow \text{hexagon} :: Count the sides for the name. \text{sides equal and angles equal?} :: Both: regular. Either one fails: irregular. \text{an angle} > 180^\circ? :: Yes: concave (a corner points in). No: convex. \text{square} = \text{regular quadrilateral} :: A rhombus has equal sides but not equal angles; a rectangle the reverse. ``` Now match the names. ### Find the mistake Read Kim's reasoning. What else must be equal? ### Concave ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time on the board: a concave pentagon, an irregular convex octagon, then why a rectangle is not regular and whether a circle is a polygon." try: { playground: board, starter: "shape.yml#free", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "shape.yml#free" hint: "One More sides click, then drag one corner towards the middle." check: { type: board, text: "Make a concave pentagon.", when: "n = 5 and v = 0", explain: "Five sides with one corner pointing in." } - starter: "shape.yml#free" hint: ["Make 8 sides first: it starts regular.", "Then move one corner a little, keeping every corner pointing out."] check: { type: board, text: "Make an octagon that is convex but not regular.", when: "n = 8 and v = 1 and w = 0", explain: "Every corner points out, but the sides or angles are no longer all equal." } - check: type: question q: "Why is a rectangle (that is not a square) not regular?" options: ["Its angles are equal but its sides are not", "Its sides are equal but its angles are not", "It is concave", "It has only four sides"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That describes a rhombus.", "Every corner of a rectangle points out.", "A square has four sides and is regular."] explain: "Four right angles, but two long and two short sides: equal angles, unequal sides." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: is a circle a polygon?" options: ["No: it has no straight sides", "Yes: a regular polygon with very many sides", "Yes: it is closed"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Polygons with many sides look like circles, but their sides are still straight.", "Closed is needed, but so are straight sides."] explain: "A polygon's sides are straight lines; a circle is one curve." ``` ### A concave pentagon Each task changes one thing. ### An irregular octagon ### Rectangles ### Circles ## Practise: polygons ```step stage: practise insight: "Names, regular or not and an angle sum, mixed; equal sides alone is the planted slip; the review keeps the polygon angle sum fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "What is a polygon with 9 sides called?" options: ["Nonagon", "Heptagon", "Decagon", "Octagon"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A heptagon has 7.", "A decagon has 10.", "An octagon has 8."] explain: "9 sides: a nonagon." - check: type: question q: "Which is a regular polygon?" options: ["An equilateral triangle", "A rhombus with angles 70° and 110°", "A rectangle 4 cm by 6 cm", "An isosceles triangle"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Equal sides, unequal angles.", "Equal angles, unequal sides.", "Only two sides are equal."] explain: "An equilateral triangle has equal sides and equal angles (60° each)." - check: type: answer q: "Each angle of a regular hexagon is the same. The angles add to 720°. How big is each one, in degrees?" answer: "120" feedback: - ["60", "That is 360 ÷ 6. The angles add to 720°."] explain: "720 ÷ 6 = 120°." - check: type: answer q: "Review: what do the angles of an octagon add to, in degrees?" answer: "1080" feedback: - ["1440", "An octagon splits into 6 triangles, not 8."] explain: "(8 − 2) × 180 = 1080°." ``` ### Names ### Regular ### A regular hexagon ### Review: angle sums ## Make: a dart ```step stage: make insight: "Building a concave kite (a dart) combines a family name with concave: the kite's properties survive a corner pointing in." try: { playground: board, starter: "shape.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["A kite has two pairs of equal sides next to each other.", "Push one corner of a kite in past the middle, like an arrowhead."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a dart: a kite with one corner pointing in.", when: "z = 6 and v = 0", explain: "For example (5, 1), (8, 6), (5, 4), (2, 6): two pairs of equal neighbouring sides, and the corner at (5, 4) points in." } ``` Then: is your dart regular? Why can a concave polygon never be regular? ## Make: regular or not, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Regular needs both equal sides and equal angles; a concave polygon always has an angle over 180° that the others cannot match." hint: ["Name it by its number of sides first.", "What does a corner pointing in say about one of its angles?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A designer's shape has 5 straight sides, all the same length, and one corner points inward. Is it a regular pentagon? On paper, name the shape and give your reasons." steps: - ["It has 5 straight sides, so it is a pentagon", "polygons are named by their number of sides"] - ["One corner points inward, so it is concave", "a corner pointing in has an inside angle over 180°"] - ["A regular polygon has all angles equal, and the others are less than 180°, so this one is not regular", "regular needs equal sides and equal angles"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why is it not regular, even though its sides are equal?" options: - "Its angles are not all equal, because one corner points in" - "Regular polygons must have more than 5 sides" - "Concave polygons have unequal sides" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A regular pentagon has 5 sides.", "Its sides are equal here. It is the angles that differ."] criteria: - "I named the shape from its number of sides." - "I said it is concave and why." - "I said regular needs equal sides and equal angles." explain: "It is a concave pentagon. Equal sides are not enough: a regular polygon also needs equal angles, and the corner pointing in is bigger than 180°." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The shape is made up for the task. Sketch it, name it, then choose the reason it is not regular. ```teacher summary: Students change the number of sides and drag corners to see polygons named (pentagon to decagon), regular or irregular, and convex or concave, and reason about why equal sides alone are not enough (AC9M7SP02, node 3). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can name polygons from 3 to 10 sides. - I can tell whether a polygon is regular, and explain why. - I can tell a convex polygon from a concave one. struggle: Checking both sides and angles before calling a shape regular. Ask students to say what they checked for each, rather than confirming their answer. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the quadrilateral family (previous lesson) and the polygon angle sum (Angles in a polygon). The one idea: regular means equal sides **and** equal angles; concave means a corner points in. The common mistake is equal sides alone (Kim's mistake with a rhombus). A dart (a kite with one corner pushed in) is named a kite by the board, as its sides fit the kite's definition; some textbooks keep kites convex and call the concave one a dart. The board starts each polygon regular (its corners are off the grid); dragging a corner puts it on the grid, so it becomes irregular. running: - "Predict: ask a 'yes' student to imagine squashing a regular hexagon." - "Run: ask what happens to one angle when its corner points in." - "Investigate: link the prefixes to words they know (octopus, decade, pentathlon)." - "Modify: for the octagon, ask how small a move breaks regular." - "Make: ask whether a dart is still a kite, and why." - "Make on paper: ask which angle is different, and why equal sides do not fix it." stuck: - see: A student calls a rhombus regular (Kim's mistake). ask: Are its angles all the same? fix: Regular needs equal sides and equal angles. - see: A student mixes up convex and concave. ask: Does any corner point into the shape, like a cave? fix: "Concave has a 'cave': a corner pointing in." - see: A student confuses heptagon and hexagon. ask: "Which has six: hex or hept?" fix: Hex six, hept seven (like September, the old seventh month). stretch: Which regular polygons tile a floor with no gaps? Use their angles (60°, 90°, 108°, 120°) to explain. support: Keep the names table visible; tick 'sides equal' and 'angles equal' separately for each shape. leads: > This completes AC9M7SP02. Where it leads: tessellations, and the interior and exterior angles of regular polygons (Year 8); Pythagoras (AC9M8M06) for right-angled triangles. exit: q: A pentagon has angles 100°, 110°, 110°, 100° and 120°. Is it regular? Convex or concave? a: Irregular (its angles are not equal), convex (every angle under 180°). explain: > A **polygon** is named by its number of sides: pentagon 5, hexagon 6, heptagon 7, octagon 8, nonagon 9, decagon 10. It is **regular** when all its sides **and** all its angles are equal (a rhombus has equal sides but is not regular). It is **concave** when a corner points in (an angle over 180°), and **convex** when every corner points out. ```
